concerns.text: Task T018g defines a fallback to a 'Curated Literature Dataset' from a placeholder URL ('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/example/...'). This violates Constitution Principle I (Reproducibility) and the Plan's 'Data Gap Protocol' which requires fetching from *canonical* sources. A task relying on a non-existent or synthetic placeholder URL to satisfy FR-001 coverage is a semantic weakening of the requirement to ingest *real* data.

Task T049 enforces a 'Fail Loudly' policy against *any* synthetic data fallback. This creates a logical contradiction with the Plan (Phase 0, Task 0.2) and Spec (Assumptions) which explicitly allow a 'Curated Literature Dataset' fallback if primary sources fail. By hard-coding a refusal to use the sanctioned fallback, T049 weakens the system's ability to handle the 'Data Gap' scenario defined in the spec, effectively making the pipeline non-functional if real data is missing.

Task T018a (derive primary_anion_cation_group) is listed as a dependency for T017 (validate_data_gap), but T017 must run *before* cleaning to determine if N < 30. However, T018a requires the data to be fetched (T018c/d/e/g) and potentially cleaned to derive the group. The dependency graph implies T017 cannot run until T018a runs, but T018a cannot run until data is fetched. This circular dependency violates the linear data flow required by the Plan (Phase 0) and risks dropping the acceptance criterion of halting on insufficient data before feature engineering begins.

Task T029 conflates the MAE improvement threshold (SC-001) and the Permutation Test p-value (SC-001 logic) into a single 'Combined Gate' that halts execution if *either* fails. The Spec and Plan require these to be reported as distinct outcomes (magnitude vs. significance) to allow for 'exploratory' reporting if one passes and the other fails. Halting the pipeline entirely prevents the generation of the required 'Data Availability Report' or partial results, violating the acceptance criteria for handling edge cases.

Task T039 calculates the Coefficient of Variation (CV) of feature importance *after* model training (T036-T040). However, FR-009 and SC-002 require calculating CV *across cross-validation folds*. The task description implies generating SHAP values only for the 'best-performing model' (post-training), which yields a single set of importance scores, not a distribution across folds. This semantic weakening means the task cannot satisfy the acceptance criterion of measuring stability across folds.

Task T054 introduces 'streaming' logic that may bypass the standard 'fetch -> checksum -> save to data/raw/' workflow mandated by Constitution Principle III (Data Hygiene) and the Plan. If data is processed via streaming without being saved and checksummed in `data/raw/`, it violates the 'Single Source of Truth' and 'Reproducibility' principles, as the raw input cannot be re-verified or re-run from a static artifact.
